summary: Independent eight-sprint OpenSpec plan to complete the language-to-ledger branch goals. Covers scope reconciliation, K exec-shim repair, native K failure diagnostic and defect resolution, lifecycle K differential agreement, authenticated source-to-Compact translation, exit-retaining SDK executor with static prover lifetime, Docker full lifecycle execution, and guarded Midnight Preview execution with canonical finality. Preserves all wider MC01-MC08, SP01-SP12, PCD, ACTUS, and DeFi program obligations as open.

scope.branch_completion: Delivers the six branch outcomes defined in SESSION-ROADMAP.md and openspec/changes/language-to-ledger-lifecycle/tasks.md. Incorporates historical merged language PR1 through PR7 (PR5 commit 1e8bf39, PR6 commit a3ada9d, PR7 commit 81bed86) as frozen baselines. Resolves K crash diagnostic findings E04-1 through E04-4 with same-author Grok repair and fresh Astra audit. Executes the admitted C7/D1/G60 diagnostic run. Resolves native K failure without narrowing depth 5947 or Core 65536 bounds. Delivers formal lifecycle K contract with 38-case differential corpus and mutation controls. Compiles authenticated Compact lifecycle contract with cryptographic source bindings. Implements exit-retaining loan executor and static PID 1 prover lifetime wrapper. Executes four-stage loan lifecycle on Docker with raw exit 0 and verified external containment. Executes admitted Preview run with canonical finality and fee-inclusive readback. Reconciles branch scope without modifying wallet identities or uncommitted user work.
scope.remaining_program_obligations: Branch completion is strictly delimited and does not grant global program acceptance or close broader milestones. Full MC01 language freeze, MC02 complete multi-asset Preview coverage, MC03 native recursive proofs, MC04 general compiler correspondence, MC05 mandatory intent acceptance, MC06 private handoff and composition, MC07 full ACTUS (277 fixtures, 32 dispositions) and DeFi (72 rows), and MC08 developer release remain open. SP01-SP12 gates, ledger-10 native certificate experiments (E3/E5), recursive history integration, and off-ledger segment proofs remain separate open obligations.

alternatives.name: K-Semantics First then Ledger Integration (Sequential Pipeline)
alternatives.tradeoffs: Advantage: Rigorously verifies Core/4 operational semantics and K differential agreement before freezing Compact contract logic and ledger constraints. Prevents premature compiler iterations on invalid semantic foundations. Disadvantage: Serializes the critical path, delaying live Docker and Preview execution until K diagnostic and corpus verification are complete.

alternatives.name: Parallel K Repair and Compact Compiler/Executor Tooling
alternatives.tradeoffs: Advantage: Shortens calendar schedule by developing Compact compiler bindings, the C prover lifetime wrapper, and the Python executor concurrently with K diagnostic resolution. Disadvantage: Violates single implementation writer constraints if shared files collide; risks rework if K semantic fixes reveal unexpected state representation requirements for Compact; splits reviewer attention.

alternatives.name: Ledger-First Preview Validation then Formal K Alignment
alternatives.tradeoffs: Advantage: Immediately exercises Midnight network, proof server, and Docker infrastructure to retire operational and network integration risks early. Disadvantage: Compact lowering proceeds without formal K differential validation, creating risk of deploying an unverified lifecycle dialect; consumes scarce Preview quotas before semantic equivalence is proven.

recommended_approach: Alternative 1 (K-Semantics First then Ledger Integration). Moriarty requires mathematical correspondence where Compact is a verified projection of Core semantics. Local PR1-PR7 source work is already merged. Resolving K exec-shim findings E04-1 through E04-4, executing the single admitted diagnostic under C7/D1/G60, and proving differential agreement across all 38 cases ensures the semantic tower (Source5 -> Core4 -> K -> Compact) is sound. The Compact compiler bindings, exit-retaining executor, Docker run, and Preview run proceed with immutable verified contracts, protecting against wasted Preview attempts.

requirements.name: Java and Nailgun User Environment Suppression
requirements.shall: The shim preflight SHALL fail closed if HOME nailgun socket or HOME Java classpath paths exist. The execution child environment SHALL NOT inherit unverified user Java configurations.
requirements.positive_scenario: Preflight detects absent HOME nailgun and user Java paths. Preflight verifies the condition and continues execution.
requirements.negative_scenario: A user nailgun socket exists at $HOME/.kserver/socket. Preflight detects the path and exits immediately with code 1.

requirements.name: Committed PATH Helpers and Helper Order
requirements.shall: The shim SHALL bind exact hashes for all selected host helper binaries. The shim SHALL verify PATH prepending order matching the actual krun wrapper.
requirements.positive_scenario: All selected host utilities match pinned hashes in exact wrapper resolution order. Execution continues to preflight verification.
requirements.negative_scenario: A host utility in PATH does not match its pinned SHA256 digest. Preflight rejects the mismatch and halts before exec.

requirements.name: Nix DB and Symlink Ownership Verification
requirements.shall: The shim SHALL verify ownership of the Nix database and query binary. The shim SHALL evaluate symlink target mode separately from link mode.
requirements.positive_scenario: Nix DB is verified root-owned and nonwritable. Symlink link and target modes are verified without false drift.
requirements.negative_scenario: Nix DB is found writable by non-root user. The shim aborts execution immediately with a permission violation.

requirements.negative_scenario: A proposed patch raises stack limit above 8MiB or truncates metadata. Verification test detects bound change and fails.

requirements.name: Deterministic Process Classification and Exit Retention

requirements.name: Prover Static Lifetime Boundary
requirements.shall: The static PID 1 prover wrapper SHALL enforce entry plus 1500 seconds and outer plus 1620 seconds limits. The wrapper SHALL terminate all private PID namespace children upon timeout.
requirements.positive_scenario: Proof server completes within 100 seconds. Wrapper reaps child and exits cleanly.
requirements.negative_scenario: Proof server hangs indefinitely. Wrapper triggers SIGKILL at deadline and tears down container PID namespace.

requirements.positive_scenario: All 12 injected failure scenarios produce expected status, exit codes, and durable receipts.
requirements.negative_scenario: An injected unpersisted startup produces PROCESS_SUCCESS. Test suite fails immediately.
